title: SingleThreadedEventLoop: add read-only iterator of channels

timeline.message:
SingleThreadedEventLoop: add read-only iterator of channels

Motivation:

For servers there is a need for per eventloop "watchdog" timer that ticks for all eventloop channels. For moderately high number of connections, It is cheaper cpu-wise than per channel scheduling.

Now this requires additional data structure to hold active channels - which is wasteful as It duplicates the one from SingleThreadedEventLoop (its practically useful impls - epoll, kqueue, nio).

Modification:

Add read-only iterator of eventloop channels exposed on SingleThreadedEventLoop as Iterator<Channel> registeredChannelsIterator()

Result:

SingleThreadedEventLoop channels may be iterated without additional redundant data structures
timeline.author: Maksym Ostroverkhov

timeline.body:
Motivation:

For servers there is a need for per eventloop "watchdog" timer that ticks for all eventloop channels. For moderately high number of connections, It is cheaper cpu-wise than per channel scheduling.

Now this requires additional data structure to hold active channels - which is wasteful as It duplicates the one from SingleThreadedEventLoop (its practically useful impls - epoll, kqueue, nio).

Modification:

Add read-only iterator of eventloop channels exposed on SingleThreadedEventLoop as 
`Iterator<Channel> registeredChannelsIterator()`.

Result:

SingleThreadedEventLoop channels may be iterated without additional redundant data structures.

Fixes #12595.
We also have `AbstractSingleThreadEventLoopTest` which covers epoll and kqueue. I don't know why nio hasn't been migrated to using that.
How about adding some javadoc and marking it `@UnstableApi`?
I think this is not thread-safe as calling values() is not thread-safe

reply.body:
It is intended to be non-thread-safe, and be called from within event loop only (same as its `int registeredChannels()` sibling). Do you have use-case in mind? IMO thread-safe channels iterator would make sense for `EventLoopGroup` and not individual event loops.

On the other hand, in tests iterator is incorrectly used outside of eventloop so that needs to be fixed.
@mostroverkhov in this case we should check `inEventLoop()` and if not throw.
